title: Executive health brief and concise stakeholder walkthrough (draft)
summary: Short, executive-oriented QBR alternative for strategic accounts: 30–40 minute health brief focused on renewal signals, high-impact priorities, and clear decisions. Built to replace long multi-stakeholder QBRs when exec time is scarce. Includes a tight agenda, facilitator script, pre-reads, and a post-meeting action tracker.
audience: Customer exec sponsor + 1-2 product/ops leads + Redwood AM/CS manager
objectives: Align on top 3 customer priorities for the next 90 days
Surface renewal risk and get a date-range commitment or next steps
Agree on 2 measurable success indicators and owners
Document immediate escalations and resource needs
agenda_items: (0-3m) Quick check-in & agenda confirm — facilitator sets expectations
(3-10m) Health snapshot — one slide: adoption, latency/cost signals, support trends
(10-18m) Customer priorities — customer speaks to top 3; facilitator probes impact and timeline
(18-26m) Renewal intelligence & risk signals — present renewal status, blockers, and proposed remediation
(26-32m) Decisions & commitments — agree on yes/no/needs-info + owners
(32-35m) Close & immediate next steps — confirm date for follow-up and pre-read deliverables
facilitation_script:
Opening (0-3m):
Thanks for carving out time — we designed this as a focused health brief so we can land clear next steps in ~35 minutes. I’ll drive the flow and capture decisions — if anything needs deeper follow-up we’ll book a separate technical working session. Is there anything you want to add to the agenda?

Health snapshot (3-10m):
Takeaway-first: here’s the one-sentence health summary (example: usage growing, latency stable, but two endpoints see elevated error rate). Then three quick datapoints: 1) weekly active request trend, 2) token cost delta vs baseline, 3) top support categories open >7 days. Pause for a single clarifying question.

Customer priorities (10-18m):
Invite the customer to name their top 3 priorities. For each: ask "What success looks like in 90 days?" and "What would cause you to deprioritize this?" Capture concrete metrics (e.g., reduce tail latency to <150ms for xyz route). If the customer is quiet, use prepared prompts: "Is platform cost, latency, or integration velocity the top blocker?"

Renewal intelligence (18-26m):
State current renewal window and any signals (usage decline, exec churn, procurement timelines). Present remediation options with tradeoffs (e.g., price concession vs. prioritized engineering slot vs. pilot extension). Ask the customer: "If we were to offer X, will that materially reduce the risk and by when?"

Decisions & commitments (26-32m):
Read back decisions in plain language and assign owners and timelines (e.g., Redwood to deliver performance plan by DATE; Customer to approve resource list by DATE). Capture a single primary success KPI and owner. If no decision, agree on the next checkpoint and info required.

Close (32-35m):
Summarize the commitments, confirm who will send the notes, and propose a 20-minute follow-up in 3 weeks. Quick check: any other blockers? Thank you.

Facilitator cues and traps to avoid:
- Don’t read dashboards aloud; call out only the signal and why it matters.
- If conversation cascades into technical weeds, park it and switch to a "deeper-dive" follow-up slot.
- When customer says "we are evaluating," always ask "evaluating vs whom/what timeline?" to clarify the comparator.
- If renewal timeline is >90 days, shift to engagement plan vs urgent remediation.

Tone guidance: keep it concise, solutions-focused, and avoid long apologies. We want to be credible and forward-moving.
prep_checklist: Assemble one-slide Health Snapshot: WAU/MAU usage trend, top-3 API routes by spend, top support categories
Pull Renewal Tracker row and attach latest notes (include procurement contacts and legal timeline)
Verify owner names and titles in participant list (AM, CSM, customer exec); add missing stakeholders
Pre-send two-slide pre-read 48 hours prior: 1) health one-pager, 2) proposed remediation options (if any)
Open JIRA/PR list for any outstanding engineering dependencies and include links
Run quick runbook check on any known incidents called out in health snapshot
Prepare pricing/flex options matrix (if renewal at risk)
risk_signals: Key exec sponsor departure without replacement confirmed
Multiple Sev2 incidents in last 30 days affecting production routes
Procurement/Legal delays beyond stated renewal window
Repeated asks for engineering prioritization without concrete business case
escalation_play: If renewal risk high: request an executive-to-executive 15-minute alignment within 5 business days
If technical blocker: schedule a dedicated remedial runbook session with eng + customer within 72 hours
If procurement stalls: AM to engage channel partner or procurement SME and provide a redline summary within 3 business days
follow_up_actions: CS to send meeting notes + decisions within 24 hours
Redwood PM to produce performance remediation plan (owner: Lena Zhang) — due in 10 business days
Customer to confirm procurement timeline and new contact (owner: Customer Exec) — due in 5 business days
AM to update Renewal Tracker status and next checkpoint date
notes_to_self: Keep this variant short and exec-friendly. Test with two pilot accounts next week. Track meeting lengths; if >40m more than twice, iterate agenda to compress or split technical follow-up. Consider a one-question post-meeting survey (Are we aligned?) for continuous improvement.
